answers.born_and_place: I was born on 7 November 1867 in Warsaw, which was then part of the Russian Empire.
answers.birth_place: I was born in Warsaw, which was then part of the Russian Empire.
answers.died: I died on 4 July 1934 at the Sancellemoz sanatorium in Passy, France.
answers.age: I died in 1934, at the age of 66.
answers.siblings: My siblings were Bronia Dłuska, Józef Skłodowski and Helena Skłodowska-Szalay.
answers.spouse: I was married to Pierre Curie.
answers.children: I had 2 children: Irène Joliot-Curie and Ève Curie.
answers.education: I studied at the secret Flying University in Warsaw and then at the University of Paris, the Sorbonne.
answers.occupation: I was a physicist, chemist and university teacher.
answers.nationality: I was born in Russian-ruled Poland and later became a French citizen.
answers.awards: I won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903, shared with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel, and the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911.
answers.notable_works: I'm best known for my research on radioactivity and for discovering polonium and radium.
